Commentary of Ibn Juzayy (al-Tashil) on surah 101, verse 1–5:

﴿The Striking Calamity﴾ is among the names of the Resurrection, because it strikes the hearts with its terror. It was also said: it is the blowing of the Trumpet (al-nafkha fi al-Sur), because it strikes the ears. ﴿What is the Striking Calamity?﴾ Here "mā" is a subject and predicate in the position of the predicate of "al-qari'a" (the Striking Calamity), and the purpose is to magnify its matter. Likewise ﴿And what will make you know what the Striking Calamity is?﴾ ﴿On the Day when mankind will be like scattered moths﴾. The operator of the adverbial phrase (al-zarf) is omitted, indicated by "al-qari'a" (the Striking Calamity); its implied meaning is: it strikes on a day. "Al-farash" is the small bird that resembles the gnat and circles around the lamp. "Al-mabthuth" is that which is spread out and scattered. Allah likened created beings on the Day of Resurrection to it in their multitude, their dispersion, and their humiliation. It is possible that He likened them to it because they fall into Hell, as moths fall into the lamp. Some scholars said: at the beginning of their rising from the graves, people are like scattered moths, because they come and go without order; then the Caller calls them and they turn toward the place of the gathering (al-mahshar); at that time they will be like scattered locusts, because locusts head in one direction. It was also said: "al-farash" here means small locusts, and it is weak. ﴿And the mountains will be like tufts of carded wool﴾. "Al-'ihn" is wool; it was said: red wool, and it was said: multicolored wool. Allah likened the mountains on the Day of Resurrection to it, because they will be blown away and become soft. According to the view that it is multicolored, the comparison is also in terms of the variation of the colors of the mountains, for among them are white, red, and black ones.

**Commentary of Ibn Juzayy (al-Tashil) on Surah 101, verses 6–11:**

﴿Then as for one whose scales are heavy﴾. It is the plural of *mizan* (scale) or the plural of *mawzun* (that which is weighed). According to the majority (*al-jumhur*), the scale of deeds on the Day of Resurrection has a tongue and two pans. Others said: it is a metaphor for justice. ﴿He will be in a pleasant life﴾. Its meaning is one possessing contentment. According to Sibawayh, the heaviness of the scales is due to the abundance of good deeds, and their lightness is due to their scarcity. The scale of a believer will not be light with a destructive lightness, because faith is what is weighed in it.

﴿Then his mother is the Abyss﴾. There are three opinions concerning this:

The first is that *al-Hawiyah* is Hell, so called because people fall (*yahwun*) into it, meaning they plunge down. *Ummuhu* means his refuge, as when you say, "The city is the mother of so-and-so," meaning his dwelling, by way of comparison with the mother who gives birth, since she is the shelter and return of the child.

The second is that the mother is the one who gives birth, and *Hawiyah* means one who falls. This is an expression of his destruction, as when you say, "His mother is bereaved" (*thakla*) if he has perished.

The third is that the meaning is: his head's mother is the Abyss in Hell, meaning that he falls into it, because he is cast into it upside down. It is narrated that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to a man, "May you have no mother (*la umma laka*)." The man said, "O Messenger of Allah, you call me to guidance and say to me, 'May you have no mother'?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, "I only meant, 'May you have no fire.'" Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Then his mother is the Abyss﴾. This supports the first opinion.

﴿And what will make you know what it is?﴾. The *ha'* in *hiyah* is *al-ha' lil-sakt* (the silent *ha'*, a pause marker). The pronoun refers to Hell according to the view that it is the Abyss, and it refers to the matter or quality by which punishment is intended according to the second and third opinions. The purpose is to magnify it. Then He explained it by His saying: ﴿A blazing fire﴾.
